policy: Every numbered mathematical result is listed. Supporting Lean lemmas justify these results or the paper procedures. Labels and named declarations are checked automatically; semantic correspondence requires mathematical review.

results.title: Unit clause cancellation
results.scope: Exact score identity for each cancelled pair of units; applies with multiplicity.

results.title: Simplifying two clauses on the same variable pair
results.scope: Exact score identity for a complementary pair sharing one literal.

results.title: Unit clause domination
results.scope: Pointwise comparison under the stated unit and binary degree conditions.

results.title: Pruning constraints from comparison
results.scope: The literal-occurrence inequality is equivalent to strict improvement.

results.title: Infeasibility by summation
results.scope: Summation preserves necessity; cancellation preserves the single inequality; a negative normalized bound rejects soundly.

results.title: Enumerating the summed constraint
results.scope: Exact rational-inequality enumeration, no duplicates, node and depth bounds, prefix/suffix bound. Polynomial rational bit cost is the paper implementation argument. The per-variable rational-cost representation used by RandomFormula also has exact minimum, membership, no-duplicate, output-sensitive node and streaming-fold proofs. Random prefix search now has a checked output-sensitive bound including rejected calls, no duplicate outputs, and initialized whole-prefix candidate accounting.

results.title: Correctness of the literal gap algorithm
results.scope: Returns an optimum original assignment. The paper also returns its score, obtained by evaluating that assignment. The Lean model permits repeated clauses as well as simple inputs.

results.title: Relative literal bias
results.scope: Correctness and explicit exponential node bound under the postpreprocessing RelativeBias hypotheses, for n>0; correctness also covers n=0. Depth and representation bounds are checked. Polynomial bit cost and space are conventional implementation arguments.

results.title: The combined comparison statistic
results.scope: Expectation, the 2B coordinate bound used in counting, and the summed-cut surplus identity. The sharper B+D step is explained by the own-coordinate and column-count estimates used in the proof.

results.title: Counting candidates from the initial gaps
results.scope: General G-squared over Q candidate bound for exactly the prefix-sum admissible outputs; includes branching-set selection.

results.title: Linear effective gaps in a simple formula
results.scope: Original simple-input assumptions: simplicity is well-formedness plus no repeated literal sets, identifying reversed binary clauses. Preprocessing preserves every effective gap and never increases occurrence counts; the original 4(n-1)+2 occurrence bound yields the reduced squared-degree estimate. Optimality, the candidate count, and the explicit (4+2n)2^((1-epsilon^2 eta^2/48000)n) node bound are checked for n>0; general correctness also covers n=0. Depth and representation bounds are checked. Polynomial bit cost and space remain the paper implementation argument.

results.title: Correctness of weighted enumeration
results.scope: Complete deterministic optimality on all well-formed formulas, including clause multiplicities, zero variables, and empty observed support. The executable procedure computes the observed support, distinct-neighbor weights, fixed input-label order and ceil(r/2) stopping depth from F; it optimizes outside unit-only variables and preprocesses the core. Preferences use the actual residual effective gap. The proof checks an earliest optimum survives the weighted-sum test and exact suffix enumeration. Functional representations recompute residuals, substitute inherited constraints lazily and evaluate the original score at return; exact identities justify these representations. No exponential-time or probability claim is part of this correctness lemma.

results.title: Random clauses on arbitrary supports
results.scope: Complete mathematical probability and initialized recursion-node bounds, with deterministic optimality on every generated formula. The original variable labels are retained: inactive coordinates have zero influence, are fixed to their initialized values, and are counted once. Restriction to nonempty pair draws preserves the comparison statistic and candidate count; its conditional product law is derived exactly. Conditioning and averaging over every positive-probability observed support, including the empty support, are checked. Final expected and high-probability node bounds assume only the stated independent bounded complementation-invariant pair laws with positive second moments and arbitrary fixed units, not concentration or count estimates. Both concrete clause models use the common paper parameters m0=4 and kappa=3/4. All rejected calls are charged and exponential bases are strictly below two. Polynomial arithmetic overhead and streamed space remain conventional implementation arguments; no machine-cost or compiler-level verification is claimed.

results.title: Gains on assignments with $h$ ones
results.scope: Exact count-adjusted gain identity on assignments with ones x=h and the signed comparison inequality for either Boolean polarity, with rational beta and its absolute-value allowance. Proved for all well-formed formulas with multiplicities. This directly instantiates countGain_eval against the actual clause score; no assumption of optimality or that x disagrees with the chosen polarity is needed.

results.title: Correctness of count comparisons
results.scope: The actual formula-input count procedure is verified for well-formed formulas, arbitrary rational beta, and every valid prefix-round partition. It preprocesses without dropping original labels, uses the n+1 count guesses (or just zero for beta=0), computes preferences from earlier rounds, streams the summed-budget suffixes, and returns an optimum original score with an attaining assignment. The diagonal correction, both flip directions, ties, and score offset are proved. Candidates are not required to match the count guess. The formal prefix condition permits empty rounds and empty prefixes as well as the paper partitions. See COUNT_GUESSING.txt.

results.title: Max-Cut on regular graphs
results.scope: Complete mathematical and recursive-call proof of the regular-graph corollary. Regular.formula encodes each graph edge by the two Max-Cut clauses and allows arbitrary unit multisets; formula_score connects the actual SAT objective to cut size. EigenBound uses the actual Hermitian adjacency eigenvalues with multiplicity, excluding exactly one eigenvalue d. For n<=1 the hypothesis is vacuous, matching the manuscript convention lambda(G)=0. The centered norm, mixing inequality, row energy, rounded two-round profile and comparison allowance are derived, not assumed. The high-degree count procedure includes preprocessing and all guesses. The low-degree branch constructively finds a greedy independent set, optimizes the unit-only residual, and counts the actual complement enumeration. regularResult is exact on all graphs. The integer degree and size thresholds are fixed for the family; regular_family_nodes proves existence of 1<=c<2 and C>0 such that actual nodes are at most C*(n+1)*(2+14*n)*c^n for all inputs under the paper assumptions. Polynomial graph conversion, per-node bit arithmetic and streamed space remain conventional implementation arguments. The noncomputable graph-to-list encoding specifies the formula independently of edge enumeration order; no compiler-level cost is claimed. Named Paley/Ramanujan constructions and their cited eigenvalue facts are not formalized.

results.title: Accumulation with one guessed count
results.scope: The deterministic analytic engine is now instantiated for actual formula gains, preprocessing, at most n+1 count guesses, and the specified floor(n/4), floor(n/2) prefix construction. The exact round order, prefix cardinality, zero first-round row profile, allowance, and node bound (n+1)*(2+14*n)*b^n with b<2 are checked. Its total root profile equals the displayed second-round profile after zero first-round rows are omitted. A positive scale D is permitted, including the paper definition D_N; n>=2 suffices for the nonempty prefix. Earlier countComparisons_correct/countResult_correct supply correctness for the same procedures. Polynomial arithmetic/space and finite-size absorption use the ordinary paper argument. Regular-graph membership is not certified here. See COUNT_COMPLETE.txt.

results.title: Correctness with hidden communities
results.scope: Checked: the concrete formula-only algorithm, including total rational diagonalization, retained representation, computed/capped spacing, exhaustive fallbacks and all projection-comparison runs, returns an attained optimum for every well-formed explicitly listed formula. No callback, approximation, probability or input-family condition is assumed. This lemma states exactness, not a running-time claim. The asymptotic hidden-community running-time result is recorded separately under cor:planted and thm:sbm.

results.title: Exact Max-Cut on the stochastic block model
results.scope: Checked mathematical core, conditional only on the two explicitly registered published probability estimates. The original SBM is a finite Bernoulli product law on all unordered vertex pairs, with an arbitrary fixed group map and symmetric probabilities. Formal minimum/maximum block variances match the paper. The actual sampled graph and Max-Cut formula have the required coefficient identity, mean rank at most k, and norm/diagonal bounds. One rational algorithm parameter, density constant, multiplier, and base 1<=c<2 are chosen before n, partition, probabilities or units. The actual formula-only search has nodes at most K*p_k(n)*c^n with probability at least 1-1/n for every input size under the original n*v_min>=C*log n and variance-ratio conditions. Units may be an arbitrary function of the sampled graph. Exactness holds on every observed input, with the ordinary maximum-cut objective identified. No hidden partition or matrix is an input to the search. Polynomial arithmetic overhead and space are conventional paper arguments, not compiler-level costs. No random-partition mixing theorem is claimed: the result is uniform for each fixed/conditioned partition, as in the paper. See SBM_COMPLETE.txt.

results.title: Bounded differences on uniform Boolean assignments
results.scope: Uniform finite Boolean-cube bounded differences; exponential moments and the tail estimate are proved, not assumed.

results.title: Random signs on every graph
results.scope: Complete mathematical probability and initialized recursion-node bounds, with deterministic optimality on every generated formula. The original variable labels are retained: inactive coordinates have zero influence, are fixed to their initialized values, and are counted once. Restriction to nonempty pair draws preserves the comparison statistic and candidate count; its conditional product law is derived exactly. Conditioning and averaging over every positive-probability observed support, including the empty support, are checked. Final expected and high-probability node bounds assume only the stated independent bounded complementation-invariant pair laws with positive second moments and arbitrary fixed units, not concentration or count estimates. Both concrete clause models use the common paper parameters m0=4 and kappa=3/4. All rejected calls are charged and exponential bases are strictly below two. Polynomial arithmetic overhead and streamed space remain conventional implementation arguments; no machine-cost or compiler-level verification is claimed. The paper explicitly types the clause-count bound m0 as an integer, matching the finite multiplicity representation; kappa is real. This clarifies the parameter domain without changing the covered input families or the constant formula.

results.title: Conditioning on the observed pairs
results.scope: The finite pair-multiset law factors after conditioning on any positive-probability observed support. The event is proved equivalent to observing the neighbor relation extracted by the actual algorithm from a generated Formula, with arbitrary fixed units. Retained pairs have the original law conditioned only on nonemptiness; the clause bound and both endpoint symmetries are preserved, and the conditional second moment equals the original second moment divided by the retention probability. Four bounded multiplicities canonically represent each multiset. PairLaw invariance under all four masks is proved equivalent to invariance under either endpoint separately.

results.title: Revealing the endpoint signs
results.scope: Complete finite-law exposure construction on the observed support: the independent base-pattern and endpoint-bit experiment has exactly the prescribed joint law of pair patterns and a uniform independent assignment. Conditioning on base patterns and every positive-probability earlier history is proved explicitly. The generated Formula score gain, its average over uniform unassigned values, and the actual branching preference after unit-only initialization and preprocessing are identified. Coefficients depend only on the earlier history; the current endpoint row is jointly fair and independent, and the assignment bit remains fair after the row is revealed and Delta is determined. Conditional mean, variance, and Y <= m0^2*d use the actual observed degree. The deviation identity, eta bound, and joint conditional law of the later theta signs are proved. List-history transitions match the fixed-order recursion. Nonempty bounded base outcomes follow from the retained pair laws, rather than being added distributional assumptions. No concentration or runtime guarantee is claimed by this lemma; the prose-to-Lean correspondence remains subject to independent review.

results.title: Conditional ranges and bounded differences
results.scope: Complete lemma on finite probability spaces, now explicit in the paper and sufficient for all applications. Exact conditional history laws, refining histories, adaptation, centering by the actual conditional mean, and history-dependent intervals with a deterministic pathwise squared-width budget. The compensated exponential is proved for the entire sequence; no independence of increments is assumed. The independent-input corollary covers arbitrary finite coordinate laws with exact constants, including the zero-influence constant-statistic case. Finite coordinate values are represented in a common alphabet. See RANDOM_CONCENTRATION.txt; the only statement change is the explicit finite-space scope.

results.title: Absolute gains and second moments
results.scope: Both assertions, with the stated constants. Arbitrary finite coefficient sets, real shifts, and positive truncation caps; the second assertion on arbitrary probability spaces with nonnegativity, measurability, finite second moment, and positive expectation. Exact fourth moments, two Cauchy--Schwarz inequalities, truncation, and symmetry. The measure bridge identifies these expectations with the existing finite sampling laws. No statement or algorithm change.

results.title: Accumulated requirements
results.scope: Complete two-term tail with the stated constants, under the nonempty observed-support setup fixed before the paper lemmas. Fin n is the relabeled observed vertex set (n=r), and C is the prefix of size T; the proved statement permits any fixed charged set with positive degrees. The actual residual comparison, truncation, exact conditional mean, adaptation and whole-order budget are instantiated. The independent edge-data law and coefficient correspondence are proved, as are mean and sensitivity bounds and averaging over base patterns. A simpler proof uses sqrt(Y) >= Y/(m0*sqrt(d)); it implies the unchanged c1. Zero-mass out-of-bound patterns are handled by an extension of the statistic that agrees on the distribution support. No algorithm or input-model change. See RANDOM_ACCUMULATION.txt.

results.title: Favorable contributions from later values
results.scope: Complete exp(-2*c^2/(m0^2*T)) tail under the nonempty observed-support setup. Q is defined from actual score gains minus residual averages. Exact edge and incoming-row identities, the fixed-order histories, conditional exponential row bounds, once-per-edge charging, the global m0^2*T budget, and averaging over the prescribed base-pattern distribution are all checked. Generic degree hypotheses are discharged using the implemented rational normalization. The paper proof now uses whole incoming rows. No independence between A and Q is assumed. See RANDOM_ACCUMULATION.txt.

results.title: Sound comparisons with approximate projections
results.scope: For the formula-derived objective in the paper and any supplied rational projection representation, every optimum is actually enumerated in an approximating run. The exact original/auxiliary gain difference and stated allowance are proved from clause scores; no unproved score-encoding identity is assumed. Any finite covering guess list is allowed, including a product of grids. The returned assignment optimizes the original score. No orthogonality or spectral condition is assumed for correctness. The numerical routine for discovering a representation is not part of this lemma. See COUNT_GUESSING.txt.

results.title: Accumulation after projection guessing
results.scope: Both sequential and fixed-round accumulation are checked through correctness and explicit recursion-node bounds for the actual rational comparison procedures. No concentration/probability bound remains an assumed input. Proved finite-cube entropy plus smoothing replaces Talagrand, and random partition plus the linear sign MGF replaces Hanson-Wright. Norm reductions, profile/allowance normalization, exceptional-event assembly, constants, all supplied guesses, and a fixed exponential base below two are checked. The paper retains the sequential rate and uses the new explicit round rate min(g^2/(32*tau*alpha^2*K_L),g^2/(8192*k^2*tau*K)). Formula-level wrappers derive symmetric zero-diagonal interactions and independence from the guess. The formal n-by-n sequential matrix pads unused rows with zero; the prefix-row matrix pads unused columns. The positive-prefix premise follows from the paper positive profile; the inherited lower bound on n is stronger than needed. Polynomial arithmetic overhead, streamed memory, and bit-cost remain conventional paper arguments, not compiler-level verification. Graph-family membership and numerical discovery are separate obligations. See COUNT_COMPLETE.txt.

results.title: Two finite-sign concentration estimates
results.scope: Both finite-sign estimates with exactly the stated constants. The first is derived from log(t)<=t-1, tensorization, flip invariance, finite-sum differentiation, the limit at zero, and exponential Markov. The second is proved for any zero-diagonal real matrix using random partition, Jensen, the exact mixed-bit product law, the Euclidean operator norm and the linear sign MGF; symmetry is not required. Positive common budgets allow empty dimensions. No unproved concentration theorem is assumed. See COUNT_COMPLETE.txt.

results.title: A common gap estimate
results.scope: Complete revised common-gap bound exp(-g^2*n/(8*tau*alpha^2*K_L)), including the exact rational comparison-average bridge, first moments, clipping, Huber smoothing/Taylor remainder, pointwise total squared-flip budget, finite-cube concentration, and parameter substitutions. The row matrix includes only prefix rows and zero-padded columns; EarlierInPrefix proves the T*V energy budget. The final theorem assumes only deterministic norm, profile and scale conditions, not a probability estimate. The paper now presents this sufficient substitute for its earlier unverified Talagrand argument. See COUNT_COMPLETE.txt.

results.title: Polynomial projection grids
results.scope: The explicit rational grids have checked coverage, Cartesian-product size, the stated cardinality and total-prefix-allowance bounds. Both analytic accumulation variants are now applied to these grids, yielding explicit executed-node bounds with the grid factor and base below two, and grid_search_correct proves exactness of the same procedure. Rational norm-at-most-one is expressed by the equivalent real-cast sum of coordinate squares. Polynomial arithmetic/streamed space remain conventional implementation arguments; discovering a representation is not part of this result. See COUNT_COMPLETE.txt.

results.title: Independent-pair membership
results.scope: Checked for the explicitly stated integer interaction coefficients, on an arbitrary original probability space, conditional only on the two registered published estimates. The previous unrestricted-real auxiliary formulation has been narrowed to the integer coefficients of every Max 2-SAT/Max Cut input family in this paper; continuously distributed real coefficients are not claimed. This does not narrow any computational input family. Almost-sure boundedness gives a finite common integer alphabet. The encoding preserves joint independence, original event probabilities, expectations and the ordinary measure-theoretic variance. Both empirical and supplied membership alternatives, the original constants/size/density, and the additional count-accumulation size condition are checked. The encoded values may have arbitrary real probabilities. No original finite-sample-space assumption remains. See SUBMISSION_SCOPE.txt.

results.title: Discovering a bounded-rank mean
results.scope: Checked mathematical core for the original independent bounded integer-valued inputs on any probability space, conditional only on the two registered published estimates. Original expectations, variances, almost-sure bounds, hidden mean rank/norm/diagonal, and formula interactions are used directly. One rational algorithm parameter, density constant, multiplier and base c<2 are chosen before all sizes and probability spaces. A measurable event of probability at least 1-1/n implies the actual formula-only search node bound K*p_r(n)*c^n. The event depends only on binary coefficients; the bound is uniform in added units, even chosen after the draw using additional randomness. Actual rational diagonalization, finite termination, unconditional exactness, density substitution and bounded-size cases are checked. No numerical callback, finite-law assumption or internal quality estimate remains. Polynomial bit-operation overhead and polynomial space remain conventional paper arguments, not machine-cost theorems. See SUBMISSION_SCOPE.txt.

results.title: A biased subset attached to an arbitrary remainder
results.scope: Research target only: the appendix supplies no proof and claims no formal verification. The proposed complexity guarantee is given a witnessing subset and scale; recognizing all such subsets from the formula alone is a separate question.
